name: Motion Film
description: Design and render a motion-design film in code — launch videos, promos, feature announcements, explainers, brand openers, social loops — as one time-seeked HTML file rendered to MP4 with Playwright + ffmpeg.
prompt:
# Motion Film

Use this skill when the user wants a motion-design film made in code: launch video, product promo, feature announcement, animated explainer, brand/event opener, social loop, or keynote-style film.

Do not use this skill when:
- the user wants a reusable editor app (use `motion-editor`)
- the request is a Manim math/algorithm explainer (use `manim-video`)
- the user is working in a HyperFrames composition (use `hyperframes`)
- the task is editing existing live-action footage or generating a clip with a video model

Inputs:
- Project brief: {{project_brief}}
- Film kind: {{film_kind}}
- Aspect: {{aspect}}
- Length seconds: {{length_seconds}}
- Output dir: {{output_dir}}

Workflow:
1. Resolve the project folder. If `{{output_dir}}` is empty, use `motion-film-project` in the current workspace.
2. Read `{baseDir}/SKILL.md` and `{baseDir}/references/techniques.md` before building. Use `{baseDir}/references/example-launch-film.md` as the quality and density bar, not as a script.
3. Brief: ask once for what is missing (project, kind, format, brand, assets, music, style), offering the SKILL.md defaults so the user can answer "defaults". Use only user-supplied or free-for-commercial-use assets; never invent product UI the user did not ask for.
4. Design: write the story as 4-6 acts chained by transforms, a beat map table (beat, time, trigger, transform, SFX), and render 3-5 stills from a stub `seek(t)`. Stop and get approval before the full build.
5. Build one HTML file at target resolution where every style is computed inside `async seek(t)`: no CSS transitions/animations, timers, `Date.now()`, unseeded randomness, or carried state. Use closed-form springs. One continuous take; no crossfades, blur-ins, 3D flips, particles, glows, or holds over 1s.
6. Sound: a downloaded SFX per event positioned by measured peak, song starting on a downbeat, loudnorm to -14 LUFS. Skip if the user wants silent.
7. Render with Playwright (4 subframes per frame) and ffmpeg `tmix` to 60fps motion blur. Check one frame per beat, scan for single-frame pops (frame-diff spikes 3x neighbours), fix and re-render, then mux audio.
8. Write run artifacts to:
   - `{artifactDir}/beat-map.md`
   - `{artifactDir}/render-report.md`
   Include acts, beats, assets and licenses, render command, and QA results.
9. End with the exact MP4 path, a few representative frames, and any missing dependencies (Node, Playwright Chromium, ffmpeg).

Success criteria:
- Stills and beat map approved before the full build.
- The film is deterministic, seekable, and passes the per-beat and pop checks.
- The delivered MP4 matches the requested format, length, and loop behaviour.

parameters.name: project_brief
parameters.description: What the project is, who it's for, and the one thing the viewer should remember

routing.useWhen: Use when the user asks to make a launch video, product promo, feature announcement, motion graphics, animated explainer, brand or event opener, social loop, keynote-style film, or to make a video with code.
routing.dontUseWhen: Do not use for building a reusable motion editor app (use motion-editor), Manim math or algorithm explainers (use manim-video), HyperFrames compositions (use hyperframes), editing existing live-action footage, or model-generated video clips.
routing.outputs: A time-seeked HTML film, render script, approved beat map and stills, and a muxed MP4 in the project folder, plus beat-map and render-report artifacts under {artifactDir}.
routing.successCriteria: Stills and beat map approved before the build; the film is deterministic and seekable; per-beat frames and single-frame pop checks pass; the MP4 matches the requested format and length.
